title: The Crick COVID-19 RT-PCR Testing Pipeline
author: The Crick COVID-19 Consortium
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfe2jjge

steps.title: Receive and Track Samples
steps.instruction: Receive barcoded swabs in collection tubes (either dry or in Virus Transfer Medium).

substeps.instruction: Unpack and track samples using the Tube Tracker (Cerebros Medical Systems) specimen management tool.
Perform a visual inspection of sample integrity.
Scan samples into the internal LIMS (Crick Clarity LIMS).
Return or dispose of incorrect or leaky samples according to internal safety regulations.

steps.title: Inactivate Virus
steps.instruction: Perform viral inactivation within a Class I or II safety cabinet using appropriate PPE.

substeps.instruction: For samples containing VTM: transfer 100 μL of the specimen to a barcoded 2-ml screw cap tube prefilled with 1 ml of 5M guanidinium thiocyanate L6 virus inactivation buffer.
For dry swabs: immerse the swab directly in the inactivation buffer.
Visually check and confirm the barcodes of both the collection tube and the inactivated viral sample.
Process only one sample at a time to prevent swapping.
Decontaminate liquid waste with 10% Surfanios.

steps.title: Extract RNA
steps.instruction: Automate RNA extraction using a Biomek FX liquid handling platform (Beckman Coulter) and silica-coated magnetic beads (G-Biosciences).

substeps.instruction: Transfer 150 μL of inactivated lysate from each individual sample tube to a Nunc 96-DeepWell polypropylene storage plate using a Hamilton STAR or STARlet liquid handling platform.
Use pre-prepared batch-certified binding buffer (BB) and a home-made guanidine hydrochloride solution for extraction.
Elute the RNA into a 96-well barcoded plate.

steps.title: Perform RT-PCR
steps.instruction: Quantify SARS-CoV-2 RNA using the ABI QuantStudio 3 system and a BGI kit targeting the ORF1ab region.

substeps.instruction: Use 10 μL of extracted RNA per assay.
Include a human beta-actin primer/probe set as an internal reference (VIC fluorophore).
Include a positive control (provided in the kit) and a sample-free eluate as a blank control for each batch of 94 samples.
Run each batch of samples in duplicate.
Run a reference plate on alternate days for quality control.

steps.title: Assess Data Quality
steps.instruction: Evaluate the integrity of the run based on internal and external control criteria.

substeps.instruction: Verify Blank Control: Ct values must be >37.0 (or no data) for FAM and >35.0 (or no data) for VIC.
Verify Positive Control: Standard curves for FAM and VIC must be S-shaped with Ct values ≤37.0 and ≤35.0, respectively.
Invalidate the entire plate if these criteria are not met.

steps.title: Interpret Results
steps.instruction: Apply automated logic to determine the sample status based on Ct values.

substeps.instruction: Positive: COVID-19 Ct <37.0 with typical exponential amplification (regardless of IC value).
Negative: COVID-19 'undetermined' or Ct >37.0, AND IC <35.0.
Failed Sample: COVID-19 'undetermined' or Ct >37.0, AND IC >35.0 (indicates inadequate swab).

steps.title: Report and Authorize Results
steps.instruction: Use a custom-made online web portal for remote clinical interpretation and reporting.

substeps.instruction: First reporter performs initial quality control and exports data as a .xls file to the pathology LIMS.
Second reporter accesses data via the web application to verify controls, check amplification curves, and ensure a complete audit trail.
Second reporter manually sets the threshold above background non-exponential amplification.
Export final results to the reference laboratory for clinical authorization and patient notification.

description: 2 Abstract The emergence of the novel coronavirus SARS-CoV-2 has led to a pandemic infecting more than two million people worldwide in less than four months, posing a major threat to healthcare systems. This is compounded by the shortage of available tests causing numerous healthcare workers to unnecessarily self -isolate. We provide a roadmap instructing how a research institute can be repurposed in the midst of this crisis, in collaboration with partner hospitals and an established diagnostic laboratory, harnessing existing expertise in virus handling, robotics, PCR, and data science to derive a rapid, high throughput diagnostic testing pipeline for detecting SARS-CoV-2 in patients with suspected COVID-19. The pipeline is used to detect SARS-CoV-2 from combined nose -throat swabs and endotracheal secretions/ bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Notably, it relies on a series of in -house buffers for virus inactivation and the extraction of viral RNA, thereby reducing the dependency on commercial suppliers at times of global shortage. We use a commercial RT-PCR assay, from BGI, and results are reported with a bespoke online web application that integrates with the healthcare digital system. This strategy facilitates the remote reporting of thousands of samples a day with a turnaround time of under 24 hours, universally applicable to laboratories worldwide. All rights reserved.
